# Verdict: APPROVE both operations, with one required post-deploy check

I reviewed this myself as Opus 5.5 and didn't run the pasted script, because the brief says no delegation. I made no repo edits, no Convex, Cloudflare or WorkOS calls, used no credentials and deployed nothing. That also means I didn't write `independent-review.json` or a decisions-log entry. Save them from this reply if you want them on record.

## What I checked

**The frozen candidate matches.** All six changed files in `ops/previews` hash exactly to `previews-r4/candidate.json`.

**Tests:**
- `node --test ops/previews/policy.test.mjs` passes 16 of 16. The saved red run (14 of 16) shows the two new tests fail without the new code.
- My own 5 offline tests pass. They cover:
  - the edges of the 10-minute recovery window;
  - changed backend identity, wrong PR, and an ID passed as text or as not-a-number;
  - an extra field or wrong name on the frontend preview;
  - the real PR3 and PR4 receipts.
- **These tests can fail.** Against a copy of `policy.mjs` with a widened window, the window test fails. Against a copy with the frontend identity check removed, two replacement tests fail.
- **The real commands refuse repeats.** I ran them on copied receipts and each refused before any network call, leaving no new files:
  - PR3 without `--recover`, or with it after recovery was already spent;
  - `--recover` with a missing ID;
  - a second `--rebuild` on PR4;
  - a plain build over the existing artifact;
  - `--replace` with no ID.
- The real PR3 and PR4 receipts were not touched.

## PR3 `--recover neat-squid-188 5678975`: APPROVE

- **Exact identity.** The recovery code checks the Convex project, that it's a preview (not the default), the `pr-3` name and address, and the exact deployment name and ID. The name must match exactly one deployment in the project list, and the deployment's own record must agree with that list entry.
- **Original allocation time.** The deployment was created 330 ms after the original attempt, well inside the allowed window of 5 seconds before to 10 minutes after.
- **Empty backend.** It requires no functions, no tables and no environment variables, using the exact CLI output. The saved before-files (`pr3-*-before.json`) show exactly that state.
- **Preserved evidence.** It needs the original `backend-deploy.log` to show the deployment address and the original failure message. The receipt is saved to `before-recovery.json`, which can't be overwritten, and the new log goes to its own file, `backend-recovery.log`.
- **Same ID rechecked before push.** In the installed Convex 1.46, `--preview-name` without `--preview-create` reuses the existing preview (`deploy.js:131`). The hook runs before the push (`deploy.js:233`, then `runPush`). The hook then compares ID, name, creation time, reference and address to what recovery recorded. If Convex handed back a different deployment, it would refuse before pushing.
- **No automatic retry.** Recovery only runs from the original attempted state, so once it has run it can't run again.

## PR4 `--rebuild` and frontend `--replace 567c0b1448364e4786f2bafb238b372d`: APPROVE

- **The rebuilt artifact passes on its own.** The release verifier accepts it against its new manifest (`e5d1610c…`). The archived artifact passes against its old manifest (`1b50ae0d…`), and each is refused against the other's.
- **The only change is the callback.** The two JS bundles differ in one spot: `redirectUri:void 0` became the exact PR4 callback URL, `https://pr-4-remold-i2-preview.shakur-949.workers.dev/callback`. `_headers`, `_redirects`, the two SVG icons, the CSS and fonts are identical. `index.html` differs only in the script filename. The new build record lists `VITE_WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI`.
- **Old bytes are preserved.** The archived receipt matches the committed r3 `pr4-reconciled-receipt.json` byte for byte. The archived deploy log hash matches the `logSha256` saved during r3 reconciliation.
- **No repeated creation.** In Wrangler 4.138, `preview --name` first looks the preview up by name (`cli.js` ~177470). If it exists, Wrangler updates that same preview and adds a new deployment under its existing ID. The code only records success if the returned ID is the owned one. Otherwise it records the preview as unresolved and throws.

## Real blocker (evidence, not safety)

**The frontend's own "success" check can't tell old bytes from new.** After deploying, `frontend.mjs` checks the served `/version.json`, but that file is identical in the old and new builds (`6e959eca…`). The deploy message it checks, `I2 PR4 c666909…`, is also the same as the old one. So `frontend-ready` would be recorded even if the old bytes were still being served.

Before counting the replacement as done, a read-only check must confirm two things:
- the served `/release-manifest.json` has sha256 `e5d1610cf4278a23d44b0547ae5d9ad46c3ea974201f18839e37dda0c331e003`;
- the served page loads `/assets/index-Z3X--hDy.js`, which contains the callback.

The deployment ID Wrangler returns should also differ from the old one, `0659e24b-988a-4945-b8d1-11cea250ec87`. Until that check passes, PR4 counts as attempted, not deployed.

## Not verified here

- Whether any provider call will actually succeed.
- The live GitHub checks the code runs itself (PR still OPEN, same head, same base).
- UI sign-in, exact callback and CORS, and sign-out.
- WorkOS entries, the two test fixtures and cleanup.

Full I2 remains open.

## Recommendations (optional, not blockers)

1. Check the recovery name's format before it goes into the Convex API path. Today an operator-typed name reaches a read request before identity is checked.
2. Make the post-deploy check compare the manifest hash and deployment ID instead of `version.json`.
3. When rebuilding, clear or rename the leftover fields from the old deploy (`unresolvedCloudflare`, `reconciliation`, `versionReadback`) so the `artifact-ready` receipt doesn't carry them. They're already preserved in the archive.

My test files are in `/tmp/remold-r4-iv-6u6E` if you want to rerun them.
